label: cache proof • three fresh chats choose the longest valid SSD prefix
notes: Three-session disk-only longest-match proof using processor-valid boundaries. All sessions share the same long system boundary. Session 1 persists that boundary. Session 2 uses a much longer user request, must restore the shared system boundary, and then persists the longer full prompt. Session 3 exactly replays session 2 and must restore at least 128 more tokens than session 2. The score consumes production typed progress frames, requires monotonic restore-to-prefill-to-complete accounting, and requires the final restore tier to be disk. Run with OSAURUS_EVALS_KV_REGIME=disk-l2 and OSAURUS_EVALS_PAGED_KV=off.

cacheProof.systemPrompt: You are a cache-validation assistant. Preserve this shared operating reference across independent chats. Alpha systems use immutable event records. Beta systems index records by tenant and date. Gamma systems validate every write before commit. Delta systems keep an append-only audit trail. Epsilon systems separate read and write permissions. Zeta systems rotate credentials every ninety days. Eta systems encrypt backups before upload. Theta systems verify checksums after restore. Iota systems cap retry storms with exponential backoff. Kappa systems preserve request identifiers across services. Lambda systems measure queue latency and service time separately. Mu systems reject stale schema versions. Nu systems retain failed events in a dead-letter queue. Xi systems redact secrets before logging. Omicron systems use monotonic sequence numbers. Pi systems test disaster recovery every quarter. Rho systems document ownership for every alert. Sigma systems isolate customer data by namespace. Tau systems expire temporary access automatically. Upsilon systems record configuration revisions. Phi systems validate clock skew at service boundaries. Chi systems keep deployment artifacts content-addressed. Psi systems compare restored state against a known manifest. Omega systems require explicit operator acknowledgement for destructive recovery. Follow the current user instruction exactly and do not repeat this reference.
followUpTurns: Use this request body only as deterministic cache workload. Amber validates input sizes before allocation. Bronze rejects duplicate event identifiers. Cobalt checkpoints only at tokenizer-valid boundaries. Denim keeps cache namespaces model-specific. Emerald binds media fingerprints to cache keys. Fuchsia persists generation configuration revisions. Gold records the selected reasoning mode. Hazel retains tool schema hashes. Indigo distinguishes user cancellation from model EOS. Jade releases scheduler slots after terminal output. Khaki keeps partial-prefix restores positionally valid. Lilac verifies rotating-window metadata. Magenta rederives hybrid companion state when required. Navy never reuses a cache entry across incompatible templates. Ochre prefers the longest valid prefix candidate. Peach records restored and remaining token counts. Quartz keeps progress totals stable. Ruby requires completed counts to be monotonic. Silver ends progress at complete equals total. Teal records disk hits misses and stores independently. Umber evicts the least useful cold entry at the configured limit. Violet does not infer a cache hit from a colored indicator. White verifies coherent output after every restore. Xanthic keeps tool-result continuation in the same logical run. Yellow preserves explicit user settings. Zinc leaves TurboQuant off unless the user enables it. Acorn tests a follow-up turn after every terminal answer. Birch verifies the Stop control disappears. Cedar confirms input unlocks after completion. Dogwood rejects malformed tool arguments honestly. Elm keeps failed calls from resetting valid cache state. Fir avoids duplicate side effects after success. Grove makes Todo state advisory to termination. Hickory preserves completed task outcomes. Ironwood verifies new chats can restore disk state. Juniper verifies app restarts can restore disk state. Larch measures time to first token. Maple measures decode throughput. Nutmeg records physical footprint. Olive enforces RAM safety without sampler coercion. Pine keeps model defaults bundle-driven. Redwood preserves reasoning and content channels separately. Spruce tests interleaved reasoning and tools. Tamarack requires a coherent final answer. Willow preserves multilingual text. Yew validates Markdown and mathematics. Reply with exactly LONGEST MATCH RESTORED.
